interpretation_notes: ?? bytes belong to NE loader relocation chains, never literal C addresses.
Global DS annotations assume normal DGROUP; far/huge and aggregate types require evidence.
Next MAPSYM public is an upper bound, not the function end.
Declared types in other verified sources are useful hypotheses, not proof of a shared historical header.

structural_extent.scope: Closed structural test extent, checked recursively and linearly; not source-recovery proof or a historical OMF/TU boundary
basis: Closed recursive CFG with explicit NOP-only gaps
No known incoming cross-entry branch or alias

target_bytes_note: Raw target includes loader-chain words; use masked disassembly and semantic bindings for source inference

compiler_profile.note: Profile is attached to the object context; it is not a per-function switch and the grinder cannot change it

reconstruction_rules.rule: When the historical code holds a parameter's value in SI/DI throughout, an explicit local copy of the parameter (register variable candidate) can be required; the compiler does not enregister [bp+n] parameters directly.

Arrays are frequently word-indexed (SHL 1 / ADD reg,reg before the displacement). Preserve the observed element width: declare int arrays for two-byte strides, char arrays for byte strides, eight-byte structs for SHL 3.

Never invent a convenient symbol when MAPSYM provides the real one: use the exact name from direct_data_bindings; an unnamed operand inside a named public array is an index into that array, not a new private object.

A matching numeric offset does not establish object identity: equal offsets in different segments are different objects, and a BSS word placed by constraint inside another object's data proves nothing.

The compiler profile belongs to the unit context (layout/compiler-profiles.json): use the packet profile as given; a code-shape mismatch that only /Og explains is profile evidence for the unit (report it), not a per-function flag to try.
